title: Trivial Conditional Syntax Translation (How vs. Why)
pattern: Inline comments on a conditional statement that merely translate variable names, comparison operators, and boolean assignments into standard words.
why_bad: Adds visual noise with zero semantic benefit. A reader can immediately parse what variables are checked; the comment fails its primary purpose of explaining *why* a zero flag implies an active state.
detection: Comments preceding conditional checks where the text matches the code keywords, variable names, and literals exactly or through synonym substitution.
counterexample: A comment supplying the domain rationale ('a zero flag indicates a pre-approved customer account that starts active') rather than the mechanics.
fix: Replace the mechanical translation with a comment explaining the domain rule/rationale, or encapsulate the check in a named helper method.
source: Steve McConnell, *Code Complete* (2004), Chapter 32 ("Focus paragraph comments on the why rather than the how").
